result.description: Global edge network and cloud platform: CDN, DNS, security/WAF, Zero Trust, Workers compute, R2 storage, and AI services, all managed via API.
result.auth_detail: Scoped API tokens (user or account-owned), created by each user in the dashboard and sent as Bearer tokens. This is the main path for third parties. Legacy Global API key (email + key) still works but is not recommended. OAuth exists for Cloudflare's managed MCP servers. I found no documented OAuth app-registration flow for third-party developers.
result.access_detail: Gate audit (1): each end user creates their own scoped API token in the dashboard. Per the audit rules, private per-account tokens are not a gate. No app review, listing or partner status is needed. Gate audit (2): a Free plan exists ('Start building for free'). The docs I read do not say API access requires a paid plan. Token creation has no plan restriction in the docs. Some product features (for example Enterprise-only zone settings) are plan-limited per endpoint, but the API itself is not paid-gated. I could not quote a page saying the API is free, so confidence is medium.
result.api_notes: REST API at api.cloudflare.com/client/v4 covers zones, DNS, Workers, R2, Zero Trust, firewall, and more, with hundreds of endpoints. A separate GraphQL Analytics API sits at /client/v4/graphql. Official SDKs exist.

evidence.quote: Determine if you want a user token or an Account API token.
Global API key is the previous authorization scheme for interacting with the Cloudflare API.
Account members may only grant account API tokens permissions which are a subset of their own account permissions.
Use the following resources to learn more about Cloudflare's REST API:
The GraphQL Analytics API provides data regarding HTTP requests passing through Cloudflare's network
The Cloudflare API MCP server at `https://mcp.cloudflare.com/mcp` is the only MCP server you need to work with Cloudflare.
Create a policy to organize the token's permissions.
